standard.title: Cohesion: repetition and word associations
standard.description: understand that cohesion can be created by the intentional use of repetition, and the use of word associations
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand how texts can be made cohesive by using the starting point of a sentence or paragraph as a signal of its theme (AC9E5LA04). They have not yet examined how repetition of key words and word associations (general/specific substitution, synonyms, antonyms) build cohesion across a text.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students understand how cohesion is built through intentional repetition and word associations, and can identify these devices and explain their effect in texts.

nodes.label: Repetition as a cohesion device
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify repetition of key words and synonyms in a text and explain how this repetition creates cohesive links across sentences.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two examples of key word repetition or synonym use in a provided text and explain how each creates a connection between sentences or paragraphs.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise how cohesion is developed through repeating key words, synonyms and antonyms across a text; explain how this threading of language choices holds a text together thematically.
wider: Analyse how repetition functions differently in literary texts (for effect) vs. informational texts (for clarity)
Examine a speech or persuasive text where repetition is used structurally (e.g. anaphora) and explain its rhetorical effect beyond cohesion
success_criteria: Identifies at least two cohesive links created by repetition or synonym use in a provided text
Explains how one example of repetition connects ideas across sentences or paragraphs

nodes.label: Word associations and lexical cohesion
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify word associations — where a general word stands in for a more specific word previously mentioned — and explain how this creates cohesion.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one example of lexical cohesion via word association in a provided text (e.g. 'Look at those apples. Granny Smiths are my favourite.') and explain the cohesive link.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and explain multiple examples of word associations (general-for-specific substitution) in a range of text types; explain how word associations work alongside repetition and synonyms to build cohesion.
wider: Write a short informative paragraph that deliberately uses word associations alongside synonyms, then annotate the cohesive devices used
Compare how word associations function in a formal information report vs. an informal narrative — identifying where each is more or less appropriate
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot identify the general-for-specific substitution move cannot deploy word associations in Node 3 production — the integration task requires this concept to be operational, not just named.

response_modes.reason: The general-for-specific substitution move is conceptually subtle — students often read past it. Making the reasoning explicit ('What does the general word refer back to? How do we know?') prevents the misconception that word choice is arbitrary.

success_criteria: Identifies an example of general-for-specific word association in a text and names both the general term and the specific word it refers to
Explains how the association creates cohesion between two sentences

nodes.label: Using cohesive devices in own writing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use repetition, synonyms and word associations intentionally to build cohesion in their own writing.
nodes.minimum_width: Write a short paragraph that deliberately uses at least one cohesion device (key word repetition, synonym, or word association); identify the device used and explain how it connects ideas.
nodes.typical_width: Compose extended writing in which cohesion is built through a combination of key word repetition, synonyms and word associations; review and edit own writing to identify and improve cohesive links.
wider: Edit a provided text with weak cohesion and rewrite it using repetition, synonyms and word associations to improve coherence
Compare the cohesion strategies used in a literary text and an information report on the same topic, explaining how the purpose shapes the choice of cohesive device

response_modes.reason: Using repetition, synonyms and word associations in combination requires integrating knowledge of all three devices (Nodes 1 and 2) into a purposeful production and editing act.

success_criteria: Produces a paragraph that uses at least one cohesive device intentionally
Names the device and explains how it connects ideas across sentences
